guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: For the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, monday.com currently expects:
● | Total revenue of $380 million to $382 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 14%.
● | Non-GAAP operating income of $68 million to $70 million and operating margin of approximately 18%, assuming a negative FX impact of 100 to 200 basis points.

desk.headline: Revenue up 19% to $377.5m, beat; profit outlook raised but Q4 growth slows to about 14%
results: Revenue rose 19% to $377.5m, ahead of the $369.2m estimate.
Non-GAAP operating income nearly doubled to a record $89.4m (24% margin) after a restructuring that cut costs.
GAAP operating profit was $31.2m despite a $10.0m restructuring charge and an $18.0m share gift to its foundation.
Customers paying over $100k a year rose 33% to 2,127; net dollar retention was 108%.
Operating cash flow fell to $20.4m as $47.2m of restructuring payments went out.

guidance.summary: monday.com raised its 2026 non-GAAP operating income outlook to $268–270m from $230–234m and tightened revenue to $1,473–1,475m. Q4 revenue of $380–382m implies growth slowing to about 14%.

points: Co-CEO Roy Mann said wider market headwinds slowed growth, retention and new customer additions.
Small-business churn is up and sign-ups are down; the CFO does not expect this to improve in Q4 or early 2027.
Large customers are spending more on AI but taking longer to buy, after a 20% workforce cut at monday.com.
Co-CEO Eran Zinman said customers want a clear return from AI and the shift will run into 2027.
The CFO said the slowdown from 19% to 14% growth had been flagged earlier.
call.source: Call coverage — Constellation Research, 10 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (10 Aug 2026)

watch: Whether small-business churn and new sign-ups stabilise.
Growth in AI recurring revenue ($36m) and adoption of seat-plus-credits pricing.
Net dollar retention, which management expects to ease, and enterprise deal timing.
